text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock ticked down just 0.1% today and sits essentially flat at $412.44, but the bigger story is the 7.3% drop over two weeks. That decline tracks directly with oil prices falling—crude dropped from around $100 per barrel in early November to $89.62 today—which matters because refiners' profits depend on the spread between what they pay for oil and what they sell gasoline and diesel for. Lower oil prices compress that margin, and the news pushing prices down has been clear: Trump administration comments suggesting the Iran conflict may end soon, which reduces the geopolitical risk premium that had been supporting crude, plus reports this week that Russian crude production is rebounding and global oil is swinging back into surplus.

Refineries are running at a healthy 95.2% capacity and storage levels look normal, so there's no supply crunch helping the refining margin recover. The two-week selloff in Marathon tracks the sector-wide repricing of oil as immediate Middle East risk recedes—not a company-specific problem, but a straightforward reflection of lower crude costs eroding refiner profitability.
